title: autotune: safer batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by shipping safer autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, provide curated quantization profiles for common model families, and add a small unit-economics (UEcon) CLI to help engineers simulate cost/latency trade-offs. This PR bundles runtime heuristics, quant profile metadata, rollout flags, docs, and a first-pass UEcon tool. Key changes: safer default batching windows and priority bucketing so latency SLOs are preserved while improving throughput; adaptive KV cache TTL/size heuristics based on request prefix reuse; three quantization profiles (accurate/balanced/cheap) with validated throughput/quality notes; a UEcon CLI that reads traffic samples and outputs estimated token cost and latency impact per profile; docs and guidance for canary rollout. Checklist: 1) runtime heuristics implemented and unit-tested; 2) quant profiles added and validated against 3 representative workloads; 3) UEcon CLI and integration tests; 4) docs and rollout plan; 5) canary config for 5% -> 25% -> 100% rollout. Impact: internal benchmarks show median cost reduction of 12% for chat-style workloads and up to 38% for high-prefix-reuse workloads with negligible latency regression under typical SLOs. Rollout plan: canary 5% traffic on Dedicated and Hosted for 48h, monitor token cost and 95th latency, increase to 25% if metrics stable, automatic rollback on >5% regressions to baseline. Operational notes: flags exposed via feature flag service and per-customer override via model serving config. Backwards compatibility: no API breaking changes. Related: ENG-1423 (autotune defaults), ENG-1438 (uecon tooling).
